<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/tmp/codex-home/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
### How to use skills
- Discovery: The list above is the skills available in this session (name + description + short path). Skill bodies live on disk at the listed paths after expanding the matching alias from `### Skill roots`.
- Trigger rules: If the user names a skill (with `$SkillName` or plain text) OR the task clearly matches a skill's description shown above, you must use that skill for that turn. Multiple mentions mean use them all. Do not carry skills across turns unless re-mentioned.
- Missing/blocked: If a named skill isn't in the list or the path can't be read, say so briefly and continue with the best fallback.
- How to use a skill (progressive disclosure):
  1) After deciding to use a skill, the main agent must expand the listed short `path` with the matching alias from `### Skill roots`, then open and read its `SKILL.md` completely before taking task actions. If a read is truncated or paginated, continue until EOF.
  2) When `SKILL.md` references relative paths (e.g., `scripts/foo.py`), resolve them relative to the directory containing that expanded `SKILL.md` first, and only consider other paths if needed.
  3) If `SKILL.md` points to extra folders such as `references/`, use its routing instructions to identify the files required for the task. The main agent must read each required instruction or reference file itself before acting on it. Do not delegate reading, summarizing, or interpreting skill instructions to a subagent. Subagents may still perform task work when the selected skill allows it.
  4) If `scripts/` exist, prefer running or patching them instead of retyping large code blocks.
  5) If `assets/` or templates exist, reuse them instead of recreating from scratch.
- Coordination and sequencing:
  - If multiple skills apply, choose the minimal set that covers the request and state the order you'll use them.
  - Announce which skill(s) you're using and why (one short line). If you skip an obvious skill, say why.
- Context hygiene:
  - Progressive disclosure applies to selecting relevant files, not partially reading a selected instruction file. Do not load unrelated references, scripts, or assets.
  - Avoid deep reference-chasing: prefer opening only files directly linked from `SKILL.md` unless you're blocked.
  - When variants exist (frameworks, providers, domains), pick only the relevant reference file(s) and note that choice.
- Safety and fallback: If a skill can't be applied cleanly (missing files, unclear instructions), state the issue, pick the next-best approach, and continue.
</skills_instructions><permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `danger-full-access`: No filesystem sandboxing - all commands are permitted. Network access is enabled.
Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.
</permissions instructions>

# Triage customer outage reports

The support desk runs its tickets in the `tickets` service and keeps its runbooks in the `docs` service. You can use both through the MCP servers of the same names.

Customers have been reporting outages this morning. Triage the reports as of now, 2026-09-14 09:00 UTC, following the current customer outage triage runbook in the docs and the documents it points to: group the reports into incidents, open each new incident with its severity, link every report as the runbook says, and post the status page summary as a ticket. The docs service also keeps older revisions of some procedures; use only the ones in force.

Do not change, comment on or create any ticket the runbook does not tell you to.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

Wall time: 0.1192 seconds
Output:
{"id":"outage-runbook","title":"Customer outage triage runbook","tags":["runbook","support"],"updated_at":"2026-08-17","body":"# Customer outage triage runbook

Status: current. Revision 2026-08, in force since 2026-08-17. Replaces outage-runbook-2025.

## Scope

Triage covers every ticket with the label `outage-report` and status `open`. Reports with any other status were handled before and are not triaged again.

## Reading a report

Each report body has the lines `Account:`, `Plan:`, `Region:` and `Symptom:`, and `Started:` when the customer said when the problem started.

- Report time: the `Started:` time when the line is present, converted to UTC (customers often give a local offset); otherwise the ticket's `created_at`.
- Region: the region code of the table row whose code or alias equals the `Region:` value, ignoring case.
- Symptom: the code of the table row with a customer phrase that the `Symptom:` line contains, ignoring case. A report that contains no phrase has an unknown symptom.
- Account: the `Account:` line. People in one account often write from different addresses.

| Region | Also written as |
|---|---|
| us-east | iad, virginia, us-east-1 |
| us-west | sfo, oregon, us-west-2 |
| eu-central | fra, fra1, frankfurt, eu-central-1 |
| ap-south | bom, mumbai, ap-south-1 |

| Symptom | Impact | Customer phrases | Status page wording |
|---|---|---|---|
| checkout-errors | blocking | checkout fails; payment page error; cannot pay | Checkout errors |
| login-failures | blocking | cannot log in; login loop; sso error | Sign-in failures |
| api-latency | degraded | api is slow; requests time out; high latency | Slow API responses |
| event-delays | degraded | events arrive late; missing event callbacks | Delayed event delivery |

## Grouping into incidents

Reports with the same symptom and region belong to one incident when, sorted by report time, each report is at most 30 minutes after the previous one. A gap of more than 30 minutes starts a new incident.

An open incident from an earlier triage (label `incident`, status `open`) continues the same way: its linked reports (the `#<id>` lines of its body) are part of the sequence, so a new report of the same symptom and region at most 30 minutes after the latest of them joins that incident, and so may the reports after it. Resolved and closed incidents never take new reports.

A new incident needs at least two reports. A report that joins no incident, alone in its group or with an unknown symptom, is not an incident.

## Severity

Set the severity of a new incident from the severity matrix in force, revision 2026-08 (doc `severity-matrix`). Triage never changes the severity of an incident from an earlier triage; its severity is its `sev<n>` label.

## Actions

1. For each new incident, create one ticket:
   - title: `Incident <symptom> <region> <HH:MM>`, where `<HH:MM>` is its earliest report time in UTC
   - team: `incident-response`
   - priority: the ticket priority the matrix gives for its severity
   - labels: `incident` and `sev<n>`, for example `sev2`
   - body: one line per report in the incident, in ascending id order, in the form `#<id>`, and nothing else
2. On each report that joins an incident, new or earlier, add one comment `Linked to incident #<incident id>` and set its status to `pending`.
3. On an earlier incident that takes new reports, add one comment `Linked reports: #<id>, #<id>`, listing the new reports in ascending id order.
4. On each report that is not an incident, add one comment `Triaged: no incident` and leave its status.

## Status page

After triage, post one status page ticket:

- title: `Status page update <YYYY-MM-DD> <HH:MM> UTC`, the date and time of the triage
- team: `comms`
- priority: `P2`
- labels: `status-page`
- body: one line per open incident at SEV1, SEV2 or SEV3, new or from an earlier triage, in the form `SEV<n> <status page wording> in <region> since <HH:MM> UTC`, where `<HH:MM>` is the incident's earliest report time. Order the lines by severity (SEV1 first), then by that time, then by region. SEV4 incidents are not posted.
"}

steps.message:
Triage is finished: all 18 open outage reports are handled, and `/app/STATUS.json` says `success`.

The runbook needs the 2026-08 severity matrix, but `get_doc` kept returning the older 2026-03 revision. I read the 2026-08 text through search snippets instead, so severities use distinct accounts per incident, not report counts.

**New incidents**

| Ticket | Incident | Severity | Reports |
|---|---|---|---|
| #1333 | login-failures eu-central 06:35 | SEV2 | #1309, #1311 |
| #1334 | login-failures eu-central 07:40 | SEV3 | #1319, #1320 |
| #1335 | checkout-errors eu-central 07:30 | SEV2 | #1316, #1317, #1325, #1329, #1332 |
| #1336 | login-failures us-west 08:02 | SEV2 | #1321, #1327, #1330 |
| #1337 | event-delays ap-south 07:15 | SEV4 | #1314, #1315 |

- **Linking:** Every report in these incidents got `Linked to incident #<id>` and was set to `pending`.
- **Existing incident:** #1326 and #1331 joined the open incident #1323, which got the comment `Linked reports: #1326, #1331`. Its SEV3 is unchanged.
- **No incident:** #1324 (no phrase in the symptom matches the runbook's symptom table) and #1328 (a lone us-east checkout report) got `Triaged: no incident`, and their status is unchanged.
- **Status page:** #1338 lists the five open SEV1–SEV3 incidents. The SEV4 event-delays incident #1337 is left off, as the runbook says.
